title: Landmark PIL Cases — Standing, Process and Abuse Control (Orientation)

content.overview: This topic orients students to the landmark case-line of Indian PIL: liberal standing (S.P. Gupta), flexible process and vulnerable-class enforcement (Bandhua Mukti Morcha), and abuse-control guidelines (Balwant Singh Chaufal). Case entries are retained for study orientation; formal ratio verification remains a separate evidence-backed gate.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Standing issue? → Gupta line. (2) Flexible process / continuing relief? → Bandhua line. (3) Abuse/screening? → Chaufal line. (4) Which proposition is actually needed on the facts?
content.study:
Core map:

1. Standing liberalisation — when a bona fide petitioner may approach for public injury or for others who cannot litigate.
2. Flexible procedure — letters, continuing directions, effective enforcement for disadvantaged classes.
3. Abuse control — credentials, motive, substantial public injury, costs.

Use cases only for the propositions they orient; do not invent holdings. Cross-read companion doctrine topics (locus standi, epistolary, continuing mandamus, limits-and-costs).

Verification gate: case identity and precise ratio remain open until evidence-backed closure.

sections.heading: How to use landmark cases in PIL answers
sections.body: Identify the issue (standing, process, or abuse). Match the case-line. State the oriented proposition carefully. Distinguish facts. Do not cite for propositions the case does not decide.

sections.heading: Standing line
sections.body: S.P. Gupta orients liberal public-interest standing for bona fide claims where the directly affected cannot approach effectively.

sections.heading: Process and vulnerable-class line
sections.body: Bandhua Mukti Morcha orients flexible procedure and continuing directions for effective Article 21 enforcement for persons unable to litigate.

sections.heading: Abuse-control line
sections.body: Balwant Singh Chaufal orients screening for credentials, motive, substantial public injury, and absence of personal gain.

sections.heading: Verification discipline
sections.body: Until the case-law gate is closed, treat these as orientation authorities, not as exhaustively verified black-letter holdings.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.facts: Access to constitutional courts and public standing.
cases.issue: When may a person approach for public injury affecting others?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed where the person directly affected cannot effectively approach the court and the petitioner acts bona fide for public redress.
cases.holding: Expanded the constitutional public-interest standing framework.
cases.relevance: Primary standing orientation; verification gate open.

cases.name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.facts: Bonded labour and violations of dignity and liberty.
cases.issue: How should the Court respond to continuing public-law violation affecting vulnerable persons?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Constitutional courts may use flexible procedure and continuing directions to enforce Fundamental Rights of persons unable to litigate effectively.
cases.holding: Petition treated as vehicle for effective Article 21 enforcement.
cases.relevance: Process and vulnerable-class orientation; verification gate open.

cases.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal
cases.facts: Misuse of PIL for private or publicity objectives.
cases.issue: What safeguards prevent abuse of public-interest jurisdiction?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must verify credentials, motive, substantial public injury and absence of personal gain before entertaining PIL.
cases.holding: Guidelines for screening and controlling PIL abuse.
